```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(width = 100)
```

geoCensor converts USGS best-value chemistry records into censoring intervals,
checks the input, and estimates concentrations separately by element and domain.
This example uses synthetic data so it can run without downloading the NGDB.
Its coordinates and concentrations are illustrative, not observations or
estimates for the named states.

## Read the outcomes before interpreting an estimate

This compact example illustrates four outcomes from one synthetic sampling
medium. The domain labels are supplied for demonstration; they do not establish
real sampling support or geological populations. Repeated coordinates illustrate
clustering. Identifiers remain text, and all reported results remain present.

```{r four-outcomes}
library(geoCensor)
quick_chemistry <- data.frame(
  lab_id = sprintf("%04d", 1:32), species = "Ag", unit = "ppm",
  domain = rep(c("varying_codes", "all_below_limit", "constant_codes", "missing_method"), each = 8),
  qvalue = c("-1", "1", "2", "3", "5", "8", "13", "21",
             rep("-1", 8), rep("10", 8), as.character(1:8)),
  amethod = rep(c("ES_SQ", "AES_HF", "ES_SQ", NA_character_), each = 8),
  x_m = rep(c(0, 0, 0, 0, 10000, 20000, 30000, 40000), 4), y_m = 0
)
quick <- analyze_elements(quick_chemistry, group_cols = "domain",
  cell_sizes = 10000, x_col = "x_m", y_col = "y_m", n_offsets = 2)
knitr::kable(quick$estimates[c("domain", "n_total", "n_exact", "method", "geomean",
  "method_review_status")], digits = 3)
```

The varying-code estimate remains conditional on the recorded coding and working
model; its semiquantitative flag still requires review. All-left data retain
their detection limits with a missing model estimate. Constant uncensored codes
have no finite positive-scale lognormal maximum, so `failed_fit` preserves a
missing estimate rather than numerical precision. Missing method information
stays unresolved even when a model can be fitted. None of these statuses turns
missing information into a zero concentration.

```{r four-outcomes-declustering}
knitr::kable(quick$declustering[c("domain", "n_total", "unweighted_geomean", "geomean",
  "ci_low", "ci_high")], digits = 3)
```

Weighted and unweighted estimates here use the same valid chemistry/coordinate
records. The weighted confidence limits stay missing. The weights describe
occupied cells; they do not establish independent observations, measurement
precision or concentrations in unsampled terrain. The remaining sections show
how to review inputs, methods and spatial support before using this workflow
with actual NGDB records.

## Export, read and analyze the same text records

Version 1.2.0 adds an optional disk-export workflow. Here the input is the
same small synthetic example above. Real exports can include all species or an
explicit selection; neither export mode chooses analytical results or certifies
their quality. The output path must be new and its parent must already exist.

```{r disk-roundtrip}
example_root <- tempfile("geocensor_workflow_")
dir.create(example_root)
example_input <- file.path(example_root, "chemistry.csv")
disk_input <- quick_chemistry[c("lab_id", "species", "unit", "qvalue", "domain", "amethod")]
readr::write_csv(disk_input, example_input)
exported <- export_usgs_chemistry(example_input,
  file.path(example_root, "exported"), chunk_size = 10)
imported <- read_usgs_chemistry(exported$data_file)
stopifnot(identical(imported, tibble::as_tibble(disk_input)))
import_info <- readRDS(exported$info_file)
c(input_records = import_info$n_input, exported_records = import_info$n_selected)

roundtrip <- analyze_elements(imported, group_cols = "domain")
reference <- analyze_elements(disk_input, group_cols = "domain")
stopifnot(identical(roundtrip$estimates, reference$estimates))
knitr::kable(roundtrip$estimates[c("domain", "n_total", "n_exact", "method", "geomean")],
  digits = 3)
unlink(example_root, recursive = TRUE)
```

Leading-zero identifiers, numeric text, missing method information and every
input record survive this round trip. The all-left and constant-code outcomes
remain unavailable. This is a software example, not validation of population
confidence limits. The separate source-record index describes file positions,
not independent sites. Source and output fingerprints document content; they
do not establish analytical reliability. See `?export_usgs_chemistry` for output
ownership, late-error protection and resource limitations.

## Start with one sampling medium

Real input tables contain one selected chemistry result per sample and species,
plus sample metadata. Read chemistry fields as text to preserve identifiers,
numeric encodings and sparse qualifiers:

```{r real-input, eval=FALSE}
chemistry <- read_usgs_chemistry("ngdbsoil/bestvalue.csv")
metadata <- read_clean_main("ngdbsoil/main.csv")
```

`read_usgs_chemistry()` requires 1.2.0 and rejects malformed CSV records and
duplicate/empty headers. Blank/literal NA fields are missing; other source text
is retained, including trailing numeric zeroes and rare G/L qualifiers. Value
validation and censoring follow the ordinary builders. Both installed analysis
commands use this reader. The all-species command explicitly parses only the
requested projected metadata coordinates and stops on invalid coordinate text.

Run soil and sediment separately. Before pooling, decide which depths, horizons,
size fractions, sample media, and analytical methods describe your intended
population. A state boundary is an administrative grouping, not a geological
homogeneity assumption.

## Build a small reproducible example

```{r synthetic}
library(geoCensor)
set.seed(413)
sites <- expand.grid(easting = 0:3, northing = 0:3, state = c("WI", "ID"))
metadata <- sites[rep(seq_len(nrow(sites)), each = 3), ]
metadata$lab_id <- sprintf("%04d", seq_len(nrow(metadata)))
metadata$country <- "United States"
metadata$x_m <- metadata$easting * 10000
metadata$y_m <- metadata$northing * 10000
metadata$depth <- rep(c("0-10 cm", "10-20 cm", "0-10 cm"), nrow(sites))
metadata$sample_zone <- rep(c("A", "B", "A"), nrow(sites))
metadata$horizon <- "well defined"
metadata$mesh_size <- rep(c("<80 mesh", "<80 mesh", "<200 mesh"), nrow(sites))

make_element <- function(element, center, lod, upper) {
  value <- exp(log(center) + rnorm(nrow(metadata), sd = 0.6))
  original <- ifelse(value < lod, as.character(-lod),
    ifelse(value > upper, paste0(upper, ".11111"), as.character(value)))
  # Emulate an NGDB export whose qvalue loses the upper-censor suffix by rounding.
  reported <- ifelse(value > upper, as.character(round(as.numeric(original), 2)), original)
  data.frame(lab_id = metadata$lab_id, species = element, unit = "ppm",
             qvalue = reported, amethod = "illustrative_total_method",
             summary = paste(original, "illustrative_total_method", sep = ", "))
}
chemistry <- rbind(make_element("Ag", 0.1, 0.08, 1),
                   make_element("Pb", 20, 10, 100),
                   make_element("Zn", 70, 30, 200))
```

The example contains multiple supports at each site. That is a reason to review
comparability, not to assume that all samples at the same coordinates are
interchangeable.

## Review reported analytical methods

The illustrative method label above has not been reviewed and must not be
interpreted as quantitative merely because it is nonblank. This small metadata
example shows documented semiquantitative codes and unresolved methods:

```{r method-review}
flag_analytical_methods(data.frame(amethod = c("ES_SQ", "ES_H2O_P", "unreviewed", NA)))
```

The review preserves reported values and validity status. It does not supply
numeric class bounds or an otherwise missing reporting design. Uncensored
coding is not the same as verified measurement precision. Batch results include
a separate `methods` table; method concerns do not disappear when count-based
review thresholds clear. Declustering counts use the observations with usable
chemistry and coordinates for that fit. No routine spatial limits are added.

## Audit sampling support and joins

```{r audit}
support <- sampling_support_audit(
  metadata, group_cols = "state",
  support_cols = c("depth", "sample_zone", "horizon", "mesh_size"),
  x_col = "x_m", y_col = "y_m"
)
support$fields
head(support$locations)
```

The audit reports recorded differences and missing information separately.
Exact coordinate matches can also reflect coordinate rounding or reuse. It
neither deletes records nor proves that matching support labels are comparable.
Unknown metadata must not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence.

```{r parsing}
ag <- build_element(chemistry, "Ag")
ag[c("lab_id", "qvalue_raw", "detected_val", "left_cen", "right_cen",
     "validation_status", "censoring_source", "summary_recovery_status")][1:6, ]
```

Supported mass-fraction units are converted to ug/kg. Invalid values and
unsupported units receive explicit validation reasons. When an explicit
upper-censor marker in a well-formed first summary analysis agrees with rounded
qvalue, a known method matches and coding is compatible, the builder recovers it
while retaining the original reported value. Missing/UNKNOWN or mismatched methods
and incompatible coding block recovery; the original value/qualifier are parsed
as reported and summary_recovery_status explains the block. This does not certify
analytical precision or reliability.

```{r join}
ag_main <- join_soil_main(ag, metadata,
  extra_cols = c("state", "country", "x_m", "y_m", "depth", "sample_zone", "horizon", "mesh_size"))
attr(ag_main, "join_audit")
```

Metadata IDs must be nonblank and unique. Unmatched chemistry rows and repeated
chemistry IDs produce warnings and audit counts. Repeated sample/element results
must be resolved before batch estimation or widening; the package does not
silently average them.

## Estimate all elements within reviewed domains

For this illustration, use the same shallow horizon and size fraction, then
analyze each state and element separately. Real inclusion rules need geological
and laboratory justification; these illustrative labels are not a universal
NGDB filtering rule.

```{r estimation}
selected_ids <- metadata$lab_id[
  metadata$depth == "0-10 cm" & metadata$sample_zone == "A" & metadata$mesh_size == "<80 mesh"
]
selected_chemistry <- chemistry[chemistry$lab_id %in% selected_ids, ]
results <- analyze_elements(
  selected_chemistry, main_df = metadata, group_cols = "state"
)
results$estimates[c("element", "state", "n_total", "n_exact", "geomean", "review_status")]
results$validation
head(results$distributions)
```

The censored lognormal estimate is exp(meanlog), a geometric mean under the
working lognormal model. Its model-based confidence interval does not account
for spatial dependence or uncertainty from a preferential sampling design.
Insufficient-data and failed-fit rows remain explicit. Count-based review flags
are added without changing or filtering estimates. By default fewer than 10
exact observations or less than 5% exact observations triggers review. These
are configurable conventions, not validated statistical cutoffs, and a cleared
flag does not establish model adequacy or spatial independence.
Distribution-comparison rows also retain analytical-method review counts/status,
even when fitting is unavailable. A relative AIC winner does not clear unknown
or semiquantitative measurement concerns.

## Compare recorded methods within the selected domain

An optional sensitivity table separates normalized method labels while keeping
the pooled outputs unchanged. To illustrate the interface, assign two synthetic
labels to the example's existing observations:

```{r method-strata}
method_example <- selected_chemistry
method_example$amethod <- ifelse(as.integer(method_example$lab_id) %% 2L == 0L,
  "illustrative_method_a", "illustrative_method_b")
method_example$summary <- paste(sub(",.*$", "", method_example$summary),
  method_example$amethod, sep = ", ")
method_check <- analyze_elements(method_example, main_df = metadata,
  group_cols = "state", stratify_methods = TRUE)
head(method_check$method_estimates[c("element", "state", "method_code",
  "n_input", "n_total", "geomean", "method_information", "review_status")])
```

These illustrative labels are unreviewed, and their assignment does not change
the reported values. The table describes unweighted chemistry subsets, including
records without usable coordinates. Missing method labels remain an unresolved
NA bucket; UNKNOWN is separate and does not identify a shared procedure. A
difference between method summaries can reflect geography, geology, sampling
support or selection as well as analytical differences. This is not a calibration
or an estimate of analytical bias. Model confidence limits retain their ordinary
independence assumptions; spatial confidence limits remain experimental.

## Review geographic overlap before interpreting method differences

Use one element and the selected sampling support/domain. Here the two synthetic
method labels can be checked on the illustrative Wisconsin Ag observations:

```{r method-overlap}
method_geo <- join_soil_main(build_element(method_example, "Ag"), metadata,
  extra_cols = c("state", "x_m", "y_m"))
method_geo <- method_geo[method_geo$state == "WI", ]
overlap <- method_spatial_overlap(method_geo,
  cell_sizes = c(5000, 10000, 20000), x_col = "x_m", y_col = "y_m")
overlap$support
overlap$pairs[c("cell_size", "method_a", "method_b", "n_spatial_a", "n_spatial_b",
  "shared_cells_mean", "jaccard_min", "jaccard_mean", "jaccard_max")]
```

Jaccard is the fraction of the union of occupied cells shared by the two labels.
Both labels use the same grid at each placement; the reported range describes
grid-placement sensitivity, not a confidence interval. An unlocated or invalid-
only method has missing comparison metrics rather than zero overlap. Missing
method labels remain explicit in the method coverage table and do not enter
named pairs. Shared cells do not establish paired samples, matching physical
support, analytical agreement or independence. No concentration or method-bias
model is fitted, and nothing is inferred for unsampled terrain.

The same audit can be requested for every element and state in the selected
example, with optional method-specific estimates kept as a separate table:

```{r batch-method-overlap}
geographic <- analyze_elements(method_example, main_df = metadata,
  group_cols = "state", cell_sizes = c(5000, 10000, 20000),
  x_col = "x_m", y_col = "y_m", n_offsets = 2,
  stratify_methods = TRUE, audit_method_overlap = TRUE)
geographic$method_overlap_support
head(geographic$method_coverage)
head(geographic$method_overlap)
```

All original components remain unchanged. The three appended audit tables are
labelled by element/domain, use the supplied grid placements, and retain
unavailable comparisons as missing. The batch default n_offsets is 10 (100
placements), whereas the standalone audit defaults to 2. These optional summaries
do not select analytical methods, change concentrations or add spatial limits.

## Assess sensitivity to clustering

Use projected coordinates in appropriate physical units. Real longitude and
latitude must be transformed to an appropriate projected coordinate system;
the functions cannot infer a coordinate reference system from numeric columns.
The example already supplies synthetic metre coordinates.

```{r spatial}
spatial <- analyze_elements(
  selected_chemistry, main_df = metadata, group_cols = "state",
  cell_sizes = c(5000, 10000, 20000), x_col = "x_m", y_col = "y_m",
  n_offsets = 10
)
head(spatial$declustering)
```

Each occupied cell shares its total influence among its observations; default
weights average 100 grid placements. Cell size should reflect sampling spacing
and the geological question, with several scales reviewed. Weights are
recalculated for each element/domain using its own usable observations.

The comparison uses the same usable chemistry/coordinate subset for weighted
and unweighted estimates. Weight effective sample size describes imbalance in
weights; it is not a count of spatially independent samples. Declustering does
not identify concentrations in unsampled terrain or correct every mechanism of
preferential site selection.

## Inspect distribution shape without replacing censored values

Use a single reviewed domain. Here that is the illustrative Wisconsin subset
with the shallow horizon and matching size fraction selected above:

```{r cdf-bounds, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
domain <- ag_main[ag_main$lab_id %in% selected_ids & ag_main$state == "WI", ]
domain$cell_weight <- cell_declustering_weights(domain, "x_m", "y_m", 10000)
shape <- censored_cdf_bounds(domain,
  thresholds = 10^seq(0, 3, length.out = 100), weight_col = "cell_weight")
shape$support
plot_censored_cdf_bounds(shape, title = "Synthetic Wisconsin Ag: matching supports")
```

Each vertical range shows the possible cumulative fraction at that threshold,
given the exact values, censoring limits and weights. It does not interpolate
between thresholds, replace nondetects with a fraction of their limits, or fit
a lognormal distribution. The bounds describe this empirical dataset; they
are not population confidence bands. The support table and plot retain method
review for the valid, positive-weight records. Exact values here describe
uncensored coding, not verified measurement precision; no semiquantitative
reporting-class interval is inferred. Measurement, sampling and spatial
uncertainty remain even when bounds coincide. A state boundary alone does not establish a
homogeneous geological population in real data.

The existing fitted/nonparametric censored CDF display can be used for model
comparison where fitting is appropriate. A relative AIC winner does not prove
model adequacy. Thinning records until a normality test stops rejecting would
remove test power rather than establish an adequate model.

## Keep recorded-position memberships explicit

The support audit can return each original metadata row's membership in an
exact-coordinate review group:

```{r position-memberships}
position_support <- sampling_support_audit(
  metadata, group_cols = "state", x_col = "x_m", y_col = "y_m",
  include_memberships = TRUE
)
head(position_support$memberships[c("lab_id", "recorded_position_group",
  "n_records_at_position", "position_membership_status", "review_shared_position")])
head(position_support$coordinate_groups)
stopifnot(identical(position_support$memberships[names(metadata)], tibble::as_tibble(metadata)))
```

The two optional tables are available in1.2.0. Groups span analysis-domain
labels, while the existing locations table remains domain-specific. Group IDs are
stable under row reordering within a cohort, not durable physical-site identifiers.
Missing/nonfinite coordinates remain unlocated with unknown group membership and
size. Singletons are not cleared for spatial independence, and shared positions
do not prove sample equivalence or replication. Nothing is collapsed, filtered,
weighted or automatically assigned to validation folds.

## Save a metadata audit with its source and conversion record

The installed file workflow reads all source fields as text, preserves a raw
snapshot and records coordinate conversion explicitly. This synthetic example
uses temporary paths:

```{r sampling-file}
metadata_csv <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
readr::write_csv(metadata, metadata_csv, na = "")
support_folder <- tempfile("geocensor_support_")
saved_support <- audit_sampling_file(metadata_csv, support_folder,
  group_cols = "state", x_col = "x_m", y_col = "y_m", include_memberships = TRUE)
head(saved_support$coordinate_conversion)
list.files(support_folder)
stopifnot(nrow(saved_support$input_metadata) == nrow(metadata))
```

In1.2.0, `audit_sampling_file()` and the installed
`examples/audit_sampling_support.R` command export the same raw metadata, audit,
conversion and run/session records. Trimmed blank and literal NA values are
missing in the analysis copy; source text remains in the raw table and membership
columns. Invalid coordinate strings stop the run before output creation.
Coordinate units/reference systems are supplied by the user, not guessed.
Choose a new or empty output directory to preserve previous results.

## Keep source-value review separate from estimation

Some best-value exports differ in numeric precision from their associated
source-summary entries. Review these differences without selecting a replacement:

```{r source-precision-review}
source_example <- tibble::tibble(
  lab_id = c("001", "002", "003", "004"),
  species = c("Mn", "Mn", "S", "Ag"),
  unit = c("pct", "pct", "pct", "ppm"),
  qvalue = c("0.05", "0.06", "10.11", "-2"),
  amethod = c("AES_HF", "UNKNOWN", "CB_IRC", "AES_HF"),
  summary = c("0.054, AES_HF", "0.064, UNKNOWN", "10.11111, CB_IRC", "-2, AES_HF")
)
source_check <- analyze_elements(source_example, audit_source_precision = TRUE)
source_check$source_precision[c("lab_id", "species", "unit", "qvalue",
  "summary_numeric_delta", "summary_precision_status")]
source_check$source_precision_summary
stopifnot(identical(source_check$source_precision[names(source_example)], source_example))
```

The row-level audit preserves original requested order, IDs and chemistry.
Its numeric differences and candidates use the input units, here pct or ppm;
estimator outputs use ug/kg. UNKNOWN labels cannot establish method association.
Missing summaries and unresolved coding remain explicit. The summary counts all
input rows, including any excluded from fitting, and no audit rows are invented
for absent species. Metadata-only grouping fields are appended if requested.

No source-audit candidate replaces an estimator input, and enabling that audit
does not change the method/coding guard on upper-limit recovery. A precision difference does not quantify
measurement error, while agreement does not certify measurement reliability.
Small examples here have insufficient information for fitting; the audit remains
available independently. Both installed commands expose the same opt-in as
`--audit-source-precision` and export the two extra CSV/RDS components. Their
batch audit requires installed version1.2.0 or newer; current command scripts
require1.2.0 so they use guarded recovery and chemistry imports.

The recovery safeguard itself requires1.2.0. Here the reported value and
summary are identical across rows, but method association differs:

```{r upper-recovery-guard}
recovery_example <- tibble::tibble(
  lab_id = c("001", "002", "003"), species = "S", unit = "pct",
  qvalue = "10.11", amethod = c("CB_IRC", "AES_HF", NA_character_),
  summary = "10.11111, CB_IRC"
)
recovered <- build_element(recovery_example, "S", to_ugkg = FALSE)
recovered[c("lab_id", "qvalue_raw", "detected_val", "right_limit",
  "censoring_source", "summary_recovery_status")]
stopifnot(identical(recovered$right_cen, c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE)))
```

The last two rows retain their original uncensored coding and a separate review
status; they are not converted to another method's upper limit. Explicit original
G/> or suffix-coded upper limits remain available without a summary. No dilution
factor is inferred or applied.

## Treat spatial intervals as experimental

```{r bootstrap, eval=FALSE}
# Illustrative widths only; evaluate dependence, domain extent, and block origins.
boot <- spatial_block_bootstrap(
  reviewed_single_element_domain, "x_m", "y_m",
  cell_size = 10000, block_size = 50000, n_boot = 999, seed = 42
)
boot$summary
boot$replicates
```

The prototype preserves repeated block draws, recalculates weights, and refits
the censored model. It suppresses intervals when blocks or successful fits are
insufficient. Software convergence does not establish calibrated coverage.
Simulation studies have shown substantial undercoverage with correlation across
blocks. Consequently these intervals are experimental and are not automatically
added to the routine all-element outputs. Increasing block width or changing the
interval formula alone has not established reliable NGDB inference.

The target also matters: a geometric mean over the observed sites, a realized
geographical domain, and a broader population are different quantities. Define
the intended population and sampling assumptions before interpreting uncertainty.

## Save a reviewable run

```{r export, eval=FALSE}
dir.create("output/reviewed_domain", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
readr::write_csv(results$estimates, "output/reviewed_domain/estimates.csv")
readr::write_csv(results$validation, "output/reviewed_domain/validation.csv")
readr::write_csv(spatial$declustering, "output/reviewed_domain/declustering.csv")
saveRDS(list(results = results, spatial = spatial, support = support),
        "output/reviewed_domain/analysis.rds")
writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()), "output/reviewed_domain/session_info.txt")
```

Record input versions, inclusion rules, coordinate reference systems, domain
choices, cell/block sizes, and failed fits along with the results. Use fresh
output folders or validated checkpoints when inputs or methods change.
